children: shares increased 4% during Wednesday morning market action after releasing its third-quarter
, which surpassed market estimates, the morning prior.

"AMBQ's 3Q26 net sales rose +110.0% y/y to $38.1mn, ahead of our $36.5mn estimate, with NG GM of 48.7% (+380bps y/y)," said Stifel analyst Tore Svanberg in an investor note. "Management cited growth in both volume and ASP, driven by three factors: healthy end-user demand supporting existing customer programs; a favorable response to customers' new product launches with more advanced edge AI capabilities across smartwatches, display-less bands and rings; and the addition and scaling of new customers, with seven $1mn+ customers in the quarter (vs. three a year ago)."
Stifel maintained its Buy rating but reduced its price target to $70 from $85.
Svanberg also highlighted that Ambiq is beginning to evolve beyond its ultra-low-power semiconductor wearable solutions.

"AMBQ continues to extend its reach beyond the core wearables franchise, and management noted that a customer began deploying the first AMBQ-developed AI model this quarter for a voice-based use case," he added. "The contribution is immaterial to revenue today. Over time, however, the ability to sell hardware, software and the AI model as one package could become significant, particularly for customers without extensive in-house AI resources."

"Customer diversification is also evident in the reported numbers, with sales outside the major customers >+270% y/y," he noted. "Moreover, the company remains on track to double non-wearables revenue in CY26 to a mid-single-digit percentage of total sales. Management expects that share to hold in CY27 and rise to low double digits in CY28, given longer design cycles in these markets."

title: Ambiq perks up as profits rise and products diversify: Stifel
